media.caption: The wordmark, drawn by hand by Karim Boumjimar, was vectorized without smoothing or correction and used unchanged across the site.

Index mode. A parallel list-based reading of the same catalog. The left sidebar carries all thirteen exhibitions in chronological order, the centre column displays each exhibition's photographs in a fixed grid, and the right column holds the metadata block and statement. Selection moves between exhibitions without leaving the page.

Mobile rendering path. The catalog enters as a curated set of representative tiles, fading in along a staggered timing to hold within the browser's memory budget. The same dispersion logic carries the canvas; selection opens a vertical reading strip with a slide-up sheet for title, venue, dates, and statement.

Canvas mode, full state sequence. Arrival logo, the tapered diamond holding all one hundred and twenty-two photographs, dispersion into per-project clusters as the camera crosses the zoom threshold, gallery view, a single photograph opened at full resolution, and the reverse path back into the diamond. Every transition shares one dispersion model.

columns.text: The portfolio organizes one hundred and twenty-two photographs from thirteen exhibitions onto a single navigable canvas, structured around physical scale and proximity (the conditions under which the work earns weight) rather than as a paginated archive.

On arrival, the catalog is packed into a tapered diamond, a self-balancing column distribution that rebuilds its silhouette as the catalog grows or contracts. Past a defined zoom threshold, the formation disperses: tiles redistribute into per-project clusters, each marked by a hairline outline and a metadata title. Selecting a cluster opens a horizontal reading strip in which each photograph animates from its tile slot to its full-resolution position, a transition handled through paired rect captures rather than a view swap. The canvas runs through two parallel rendering paths, DOM on desktop and WebGL on mobile, sharing a single store and dispersion model, with image loading staggered along the entry sequence to stay within mobile memory budgets.
